data.gender_notes: Ikshithansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ikshithansh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Ikshita' (wished for) and 'Ansh' (manifestation or form). This name is believed to represent Lord Shiva's manifestation in the form of a child, evoking feelings of divine protection and strength. The name Ikshithansh carries the meaning “Lord Shiva's manifestation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ikshithansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord shiva's manifestation and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ikshithansh" is often used in Hindu society, particularly in South Indian communities. It holds a deep cultural importance as it is associated with Lord Shiva, one of the major deities in Hinduism. The infant form of Lord Shiva manifested as Ikshithansh serves as a symbol of love, protection, and strength, reminding us of the divine power that can be invoked in times of need.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ikshithansh represents the embodiment of pure divine energy, as Lord Shiva is known for his role as the destroyer and creator of the universe. This name encompasses the closeness and love of the deity towards his devotees, offering spiritual comfort, guidance, and protection. The name "Ikshithansh" is believed to bring a sense of peace and serenity, as it reminds us of the all-encompassing presence of the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ikshithansh: Radiance of the supreme consciousness, embodiment of wisdom and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Ikshvaku dynasty was a solar dynasty in ancient India, mentioned in Hindu scriptures and Puranas. Ikshansh was a king of this dynasty, the great-grandson of Rama, and the father of Vibhishana.

Ikshansh is also mentioned in the Jain text, 'Harivamsa Purana', as a king of Ayodhya who was a great devotee of Lord Mahavira. It is said that Ikshansh became a Jain ascetic after the death of his wife and ruled over Ayodhya as a Jain monarch.
